clue.text: Process whereby solicitor and client both get fees'

definitions.text: Process whereby solicitor and client both get fees

parts.words: Process whereby solicitor and client both get fees
parts.note: fee has two senses: the lawyer's payment and the estate in land (a fee simple) that the buyer receives in a property transfer

explanation.surface: A cynical remark about a legal procedure that leaves both lawyer and client paid.
explanation.walkthrough: In law a 'fee' is also an inheritable estate in land, so in a property sale the client gets the fee (the land) while the solicitor gets the fee (the bill).
explanation.definitionFit: Transferring the legal title of land or houses from seller to buyer is the solicitor's process by that name.

clue.text: Elijah's mount consumes a sweet

indicators.note: the mountain's name eats up the letter, so it is placed inside

parts.note: Mount Carmel is where Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal

explanation.surface: The prophet's horse eats a sugary treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like Elijah's steed but is the mountain, Carmel, of the Bible story; 'consumes' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a toffee-like confection of boiled sugar and butter.

clue.text: They ask for trouble: who stick them out.

definitions.text: They ask for trouble: who stick them out.

parts.words: They ask for trouble: who stick them out.
parts.note: those who stick out a body part between head and shoulders are said to be asking for trouble

explanation.surface: A warning that people who take risks invite problems.
explanation.walkthrough: To stick one's neck out is to take a risk, so the people who do so are asking for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of risking oneself is to put the part joining head to body on the line.

clue.text: Go west for one example of pill-sugaring

definitions.text: Go west for one example of pill-sugaring

parts.words: Go west for one example of pill-sugaring
parts.note: go west is a soft way of saying die, and sugaring the pill means making something unpleasant sound nicer

explanation.surface: Advice to travel west with a remark about sweetening medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go west' is slang for to die; a gentle phrase for a hard truth is the sugar coating on a bitter pill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild word substituted for a harsh one sweetens unpleasant news, like sugar coating on a pill.

clue.text: Salt from a chimney

parts.note: lum is a Scots and northern word for a chimney

explanation.surface: Salty deposits collected from a smokestack.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is the Scots word for chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Alum is a double sulphate used in dyeing and tanning, a type of salt in chemistry.

clue.text: Not that such errors' involve defrocking

definitions.text: Not that such errors' involve defrocking

parts.words: Not that such errors' involve defrocking
parts.note: office slips by a typist are named with a word that also means relating to the clergy, who can be defrocked

explanation.surface: A remark that minor office mistakes do not get a priest dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective for an office slip is also the adjective for the clergy, so the clue reassures that such errors carry no priestly penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerical errors are office copying slips; the same adjective refers to clergy.

clue.text: Is this foot-loose fellow sane ? On the contrary

definitions.text: Is this foot-loose fellow sane ? On the contrary

parts.words: Is this foot-loose fellow sane ? On the contrary
parts.note: the wanderer's title split in two reads as a denial of madness

explanation.surface: A question about the sanity of a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO MAD, the wanderer's name denies madness: the question 'is he sane?' gets the contrary-sounding answer 'no, mad' that in fact means not mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a wanderer with no fixed home, a footloose fellow.

clue.text: You need more than tires. to make cars go

definitions.text: You need more than tires. to make cars go

parts.words: You need more than tires. to make cars go
parts.note: tires is read as weary and as wheel rims, while a stronger word for wearing out is also the car's gas outlet pipes

explanation.surface: Wheels alone will not make a car work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tires' means wears out; something that more than tires wears out completely, and cars also need these pipes to vent gases.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear out completely is to drain, and the vent pipes for engine fumes carry the same word.

clue.text: Burns's Mary loses her head in prayer

indicators.note: the name of Mary drops its first letter, its head

parts.note: Mary Morison is the subject of a Robert Burns love song

explanation.surface: The poet's sweetheart is beheaded while praying.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns, the Scottish poet, wrote 'Mary Morison'; 'loses her head' drops the M.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old poetic word for a prayer.

clue.text: Recovery causes ecstatic delight round the City

indicators.note: the word for ecstatic delight is placed round the abbreviation for the City

parts.note: rapture is ecstatic delight
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Getting something back brings joy in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts RAPTURE around EC, the postal district of the City of London, its square mile of banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking back what was lost is a recovery; the noun and the verb share one form.

clue.text: A good one is a social asset -at a cocktail party

definitions.text: A good one is a social asset -at a cocktail party

parts.words: A good one is a social asset -at a cocktail party
parts.note: first read as a sociable guest who circulates well, then as the soda or tonic added to spirits at the bar

explanation.surface: Advice on what makes a successful guest at a drinks party.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'good' one is a person who chats easily with strangers; at a cocktail party it is also the soft drink poured into the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociable person and a soft drink added to spirits both take this name.

clue.text: Mr French enquired what sort of ball it was

definitions.text: what sort of ball it was

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, French for Mr
asked means enquired

explanation.surface: A Frenchman asks what kind of dance was held.
explanation.walkthrough: The def describes a type of ball: one where guests wear disguises over their faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball where guests disguise their faces is the classic masquerade, named for the face coverings.

clue.text: Storm maiden with lots of uplift?

parts.note: wind is a storm
a lass is a maiden

explanation.surface: A young woman in a gale finds herself lifted off her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the winch that hauls loads upward; 'uplift' sounds like spiritual encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum winch hauls heavy loads such as anchors upward, giving plenty of lift.

clue.text: Arcade-a fabulous king has one in Georgia

parts.note: King Log is the ruler sent to the frogs in Aesop's fable

indicators.note: the word for one is set inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A legendary monarch owns a colonnade in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means from a fable: in Aesop the frogs ask Zeus for a king and are given a log.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggia is an open-sided gallery of arches, essentially a covered arcade.

clue.text: Umber butterfly

definitions.meaning: umber is an old name for a freshwater fish of the salmon family
a brown butterfly of heaths and chalk downs shares the name

explanation.surface: A brown-coloured butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a silvery game fish once called umber and a brown satyrid butterfly.

clue.text: Spearman's novel cheese

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A man called Spearman has invented a new kind of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges SPEARMAN; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian grating cheese from around Parma.

clue.text: Like marble ? More a content of limy clay

indicators.note: the words more and a form the contents held inside the clay word

parts.note: marl is a soil of clay and lime

explanation.surface: A remark that marble is more like the stuff of limy clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' puts MOREA inside MARL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmoreal is a literary adjective meaning made of or resembling marble.

clue.text: Something burning in Jones's. locker? No, in mine

definitions.text: Something burning in Jones's. locker? No, in mine

parts.words: Something burning in Jones's. locker? No, in mine
parts.note: Davy Jones's locker is the seabed, but the burning thing meant is a miner's safety light carrying the same first name

explanation.surface: A quip about a flame at the bottom of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Davy Jones's locker is the sea floor; the clue swaps to the coal mine, where Humphry Davy's safety light burns.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphry Davy's enclosed safety lantern let miners carry a flame without igniting firedamp.

clue.text: Mrs Mopp goes to man about one Shakespeare part

parts.note: Mrs Mopp was the charwoman in the wartime radio show ITMA, so stands for a char

indicators.note: the word man goes about the numeral for one

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady visits a man to talk about a role in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Mopp was the cleaner in ITMA, a wartime British radio comedy, so she stands for a cleaning woman; 'about' wraps the word man around the numeral for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmian is Cleopatra's attendant in Antony and Cleopatra, a role in that play.

clue.text: Colonel at this point gives advice in sticky 'situation

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, such as a colonel
here means at this point

explanation.surface: An officer arrives with counsel in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads the answer as an imperative: the advice to stick together in a sticky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick together is to cohere, so urging it is advice for a sticky situation.

clue.text: Half the crew missing at the river-a time of danger

indicators.note: only half of the word crew is kept, its first two letters

parts.note: the Isis is the Thames as it flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: Half of a boat crew goes missing on the river, a perilous moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name of the Thames at Oxford, where the rowing crews train; 'Half the' keeps CR of CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a turning point of acute danger or difficulty.

clue.text: Was Percy a conchy?

parts.note: conchy is slang for a conscientious objector, but here means full of shells, as conches are

explanation.surface: A question whether a man called Percy refused to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'conchy' is a conscientious objector; read as conch-like, it means shell-like, the surname of the Romantic poet Percy Bysshe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romantic poet Percy Bysshe's surname also reads as an adjective for full of shells.

clue.text: Time off for his lady love perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that these letters might be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man takes leave to spend with his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles HIS, LADY and O (love, the zero score in tennis).
explanation.definitionFit: Holidays are periods of leave away from work or school.

clue.text: Wing that got Daedalus started

parts.note: a triangular aircraft wing is named for the Greek letter that begins the inventor's name

explanation.surface: Daedalus, the mythical inventor, took off on artificial wings.
explanation.walkthrough: Daedalus made wings to escape Crete; his name starts with D, the Greek letter of that name, which also names a triangular aircraft wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter D names a swept triangular aircraft wing.

clue.text: Gunner splits breakwater-that's the spirit!

indicators.note: the gunner abbreviation goes in and splits the breakwater word apart

parts.note: a mole is a stone pier or breakwater
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: An artilleryman bursts through a sea wall, to cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the stock crossword gunner; 'splits' puts it inside MOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and enthusiasm of a group, its fighting spirit.

clue.text: Room to 'describe the shape of Keats's urn

definitions.meaning: a room at the top of a house under the roof

definitions.text: describe the shape of Keats's urn
definitions.meaning: Keats's Ode on a Grecian Urn addresses it as 'O ... shape', ... meaning Athenian

explanation.surface: A space in the house to describe a famous poem's vase.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft room under the roof, and the Athenian style Keats names in his ode.

clue.text: They go the rounds in it, however square '

definitions.text: They go the rounds in it, however square '

parts.words: They go the rounds in it, however square '
parts.note: boxers fight rounds in an enclosure which, despite the round-sounding name, is square

explanation.surface: People go round in circles in a square place.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing contests are fought in rounds inside a roped square still called by a word meaning circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxing arena is a roped square yet keeps the name for a circle.

clue.text: Girl with right and left left and right-to do with kidneys

indicators.note: the R and L are placed on the left and right of the girl's name

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tangle of directions about a girl, ending in something medical.
explanation.walkthrough: The R and L go on the left and right of ENA respectively, wrapping the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the medical adjective for anything relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: Latin meal could be nutritious

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may become something else when reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman dinner might be good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges LATIN MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimental means providing food or nourishment, from the same root as alimentary.

clue.text: With the casual euphoria of one quitting after breaking the bank ?

definitions.text: With the casual euphoria of one quitting after breaking the bank ?

parts.words: With the casual euphoria of one quitting after breaking the bank
parts.note: a gambler who breaks the bank is cheerful (happy), leaves the table (go) and has been fortunate (lucky)

explanation.surface: The carefree mood of a gambler who walks away after winning everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The three parts of the hyphenated phrase each describe the winner: cheerful, departing, fortunate.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree and easygoing, the attitude of someone who trusts that things will turn out well.
